items.label: FIGURE 3C.1
items.title: Regional and urban-rural differences in access to water
items.content: The figure consists of two panels: Panel a (Regional differences) and Panel b (Urban-rural differences). Panel a is a horizontal bar chart showing 'Access to basic drinking water (%)' (dark blue) and 'Access to basic sanitation services (%)' (gold) across eight regions/groups: World, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, North America, Middle East and North Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, Europe and Central Asia, and East Asia and Pacific. Panel b is a scatter/line chart showing 'Population with basic drinking water access (%)' for countries ranked by water access. It uses a legend with 'Rest of the world' (blue line), 'Sub-Saharan Africa' (red line), 'Rural' (red circle), and 'Urban' (blue circle). Source: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme 2024 data, accessed through the World Development Indicators, https://databank.worldbank.org/source/world-development-indicators. Note: Panel a shows the population with access to basic drinking water and basic sanitation services. Panel b shows the share of urban and rural populations with access to basic drinking water by country. Solid red lines indicate that the country is located in Sub-Saharan Africa. Blue lines indicate that the country is outside Sub-Saharan Africa.
